Privacy Policy — Malisa

Last updated: June 18, 2026.

Malisa - AI web site Translator ("Malisa", "the extension") translates web pages and offers optional AI features (chat, summarize, explain, read-aloud) using services you configure. Malisa has no servers of its own for translation or chat, collects no analytics, and does not sell or share your data for advertising.

What data is processed, and when

  • Page translation — when you click Translate (popup, context menu, or floating icon), visible page text is sent in batches to the translation provider you selected (or the configured fallback provider).
  • Selection translation — when you select text and use the Malisa popup or context menu, the selected text is sent to the selected provider.
  • Chat, Summarize, Explain — messages you type, plus optional page context (page text and the page URL) when you enable "Include page content", are sent to the chat provider configured in Options → Chatbot. Selection actions send only the selected text unless page context is enabled.
  • Voice input — when you tap the microphone, audio is recorded locally and sent to the transcription provider you configured (OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions). If the browser's built-in speech recognition is used instead, recognition is performed by the browser vendor's service (e.g. Google in Chrome) — it is not an offline feature.
  • Read-aloud (TTS) — text is sent to the speech provider you configured (Google, Gemini, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Azure, AWS Polly, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint). The "Browser voice" option uses the local speechSynthesis API and sends nothing.
  • API keys & settings — stored in browser.storage.local on your device. This is browser-managed local storage: it is not an encrypted vault, and keys are stored in plaintext on disk protected only by your OS/browser profile security. Content scripts receive a redacted copy (public_settings) that masks keys, secrets and e-mail addresses. Keys are sent only to the provider they belong to — never to a different provider.
  • Translation cache — translations are cached locally in browser.storage.local (capped at 5,000 entries) to speed up repeat translations. Clear it in Options.
  • Chat history — kept in sessionStorage for the current tab session only (latest 60 messages) and sent back to the chat provider as context for follow-up messages. It is cleared when the tab closes or via "Clear history".

What Malisa does not do

  • No analytics, telemetry, crash reporting, or usage tracking.
  • No selling or sharing data with third parties for marketing.
  • No proprietary backend servers for translation, chat, or speech.
  • No reading of password fields or form input values during page translation.

Third-party services

Malisa sends content only to services you explicitly configure and initiate:

  • Translation providers — Google Translate (web/Cloud), MyMemory, Lingva, LibreTranslate (hosted or self-hosted), DeepL, Azure Translator, Yandex, Baidu.
  • Fallback providers — if enabled, text that fails on the primary provider is retried on your chosen fallback providers. Only use fallbacks you trust, because the same text is sent to them.
  • Chat providers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, xAI (Grok), Ollama (local).
  • Speech providers — Google TTS, Gemini TTS, ElevenLabs, OpenAI TTS, Azure Speech, AWS Polly, custom OpenAI-compatible TTS endpoints.
  • Transcription — OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions endpoints, or the browser's built-in speech recognition (browser vendor service).
  • Self-hosted endpoints — Ollama, LibreTranslate, Lingva and custom TTS/transcription URLs you enter yourself. Remote endpoints must use HTTPS; plain HTTP is accepted only for localhost and private-network addresses.

Each provider's own privacy policy and terms apply to the data it receives. Malisa does not control or warrant their retention practices.

Permissions

  • storage — settings, API keys, translation cache (all local).
  • activeTab — access the current tab only when you invoke an action.
  • scripting — inject the content script for translation/chat on demand.
  • contextMenus — "Translate selection" / "Translate page" menu items.
  • Host permissions — network access only to the provider APIs listed above (plus localhost for self-hosted services). Optional host permissions let you approve additional self-hosted endpoints at runtime.
  • Microphone — used only while you hold/request voice input; audio tracks are stopped when recording ends or is cancelled.

Retention & deletion

  • Cache: capped at 5,000 entries; clear via Options → "Clear translation cache".
  • Chat history: per-tab session only; "Clear history" / "New chat" removes it immediately and deleted messages are not sent as context.
  • API keys: remove them in Options → Providers; they are also deleted on uninstall.
  • All local data is removed when you uninstall the extension or clear the extension's site data in your browser settings.
